INTRODUCTION

The instrument panel is inside the B-CAN and is called the NQS (Instrument Panel Node).

The signals concerned with systems on the C-CAN are made available to the NQS by the Body Computer Node via an interface known as a Gateway.

The task of the NQS is to display the vehicle operating parameters and to notify the driver of any possible faults in the on-board electronic systems.

The instrument panel includes a TN LCD display and a reconfigurable DSTN dot-matrix display (HIGH version).

Diagnosis

The diagnosis of the instrument panel can be carried out using the diagnostic equipment available in the network (Examiner or Examiner plus).

The diagnostic socket is located in the EOBD, the line used is the B-CAN line.

The following operations are included in the diagnosis:

  • Display of possible errors present in the instrument panel,
  • Memorizing milometer mileage.
  • Set kilometres for the SERVICE function (instrument panel replacement)
  • Carry out the active diagnosis in order to check the operation of the instrument panel

When the panel is replaced the alignment of the PROXI should always be carried out (using the specific program); if it is not, then the mileometer will flash and the panel will not be fully operational.

OPERATION

The task of the instrument panel node is to:

  • Receive and transmit information on the B-CAN
  • Manage the accessory functions.
  • Receive and manage signals not from network
  • Display the vehicle operating statuses

The functions involving the Instrument Panel Node are listed below:

SPEEDOMETER

The instrument panel receives speed information, expressed in km/h, via the B-CAN line and then displays it by means of a pointer which is moved by a step motor.

The speed information comes from the NBC and the latter calculates the speed using the wheel rpm signal from the NFR (ABS) and measurement of the wheel circumference memorized in the NBC

The pointer remains stationary, in the rest position, at speeds of between 0 and 4 km/h. The speed signal received is shown at higher speeds.

Error conditions

In case of error, the speedometer pointer will position itself on the zero speed notch (rest position) and remain in this position for as long as the fault persists.

Speed limit (only high version)

It is possible set a speed limit from the Menu, with a range from 30 to 250 km/h

Limit selection is closed loop (not rolling: reach limit and go back). When the selection has been made and the function is active, if vehicle speed exceeds the preset limit of +1 km/h, the matrix display shows a + symbol warning message and an acoustic signal is activated (Alarm beep 1).

The alarm signal remains active (message up to 20s, afterwards only the symbol) as long as the speed is lower than 5 km/h below the alarm activation speed.

EXAMPLE

If a limit of 170 km/h is selected, the signal (message + symbol + alarm beep) is activated at speeds equal to 171 km/h and deactivated at vehicle speeds equal to 166 km/h.

ODOMETER

The display contains 7 segments and is configured as a quasi dot matrix to obtain a dot matrix-like configuration.

The panel receives information, from the B-CAN line, on the distance travelled processed by the NBC using information coming from the NFR and it increases the total milometer and trip meter counters.

The km travelled are shown on an LCD display (1) that shows headlamp alignment adjustment information.

The display lighting is green and there is an SMD LED.

The LCD has 6 digits (with 7 segments for each digit) for the total reading and 4 digits plus a decimal point for the trip reading. Insignificant zeros are not displayed in order to reduce the numbers shown to the important ones only.

When the "0 km" key is pressed (outside the NQS) for longer than 1s < t < 3 s the partial odometer is reset, but not the total odometer, the distance travelled (Trip) or the Service mileage.

The instrument memorizes the total mileage so that if the battery is disconnected (+30) not more than +/1 km is lost whilst the trip meter memory is lost altogether.

When the instrument with LCD odometer is delivered to the assembly factory the milometer can only be zeroed once within the first 200 km (or 125 miles).

The possibility of carrying out this zeroing is indicated on the LCD by the letter "H" at the first digit (with 7 segments) on the left of the milometer.

If the above operation is carried out before reaching 200 km, the total odometer resets to zero (the partial odometer reesets, the trip counter resets and the Service mileage resets) by pressing the "0 km" key for time t > 10 s and the letter H disappears.

If this operation is not carried out, when 200 km is reached/exceeded, the letter H disappears and the mileage is displayed with no possiblity of zeroing the milometer any more.

The instrument allows the programming of the total number of km (if it is replaced) on condition that the figure entered is higher than the last value memorized

When the maximum mileage is reached on the milometer (699999 km - 399999 miles), it is not zeroed but horizontal bars/dashes are displayed. When the trip meter reaches 999.9 Km, it returns to 0.0

Behaviour of mileometer with the key out

With the ignition switched off, nothing is shown on the display; in this case the "0km" key has no function, when one of the front doors (left/right) is opened/closed the milometer will light up and display the trip meter and total mileage information for a certain time.

Error conditions

In case of error, the odometer displays the last valid value until it receives a new valid value.

REV COUNTER

The panel receives rpm information supplied to the network by the NCM via the B-CAN line and displays it by means of a pointer moved by a step motor.

The panel processes the engine rpm data without corrections applying a time constant of 200 ms so that the response to the zero RPM - full scale defection RPM step is less than 2 seconds

Pointer position at key-off

At key-off, the pointer is set to 0 (0 rpm).

Examples of errors

In case of error, the pointer sets itself to ZERO (beginning of scale) until the error status disappears.

Alarm signals

If the pointer reaches the red danger area, if partial panel lighting has been set, it is adjusted to the required level using the dimmer.

For temperatures of T = 50 °C, the pointer should be at the first reference on the scale (start of scale).

For temperatures between 50 ÷ 80 °C the pointer should increase in a linear fashion.

For temperatures between 80 ÷ 100 °C (normal operation), the pointer should remain in a stable position in the centre of the scale.

For temperatures between 100 ÷ 120 °C (uphill) and between 115 ÷ 100 °C (downhill) the pointer should move in a linear fashion.

For temperatures of T = 120 ± 1 °C, the pointer should be located at the beginning of the red sector of the scale.

For temperatures of T = 122 °C the pointer should reach the position corresponding to the beginning of the red sector and, as soon as the engine management control unit sends the warning light on signal, it should be positioned at the end of the scale (t = 1 s); the engine coolant temperature overheating warning light should come on at the same time.

In addition:

  • if the warning light on signal coming from the c.c.m. remains in the ON state, the pointer should remain at the end of the scale and the warning light should remain on;
  • if the c.c.m sends the warning light off signal (when the temperature goes below the level usually equal to T = 115 ± 1°C), the instrument panel should instantly switch the coolant overheating warning light off and the pointer should place itself (t = 1 s) in the position corresponding to the (actual) temperature value measured.

There is a hysteresis of 5 °C, in other words, for example, the warning light is switched on at 120°C, it is switched off at 115 °C.

Engine coolant overheating warning light

The panel receives the information that the warning light is switched on/off via the B-CAN line.

The software strategy that regulates the switching on/off of the engine coolant overheating warning light and the operation of the pointer in the end of scale position when the temperature levels/limits are reached, both in normal operation and if there is a burst of heat, is contained inside the engine management control unit.

Error conditions/diagnosis

The instrument panel warning light is activated at each key-on (check stage); after 4 secs. the CCM/NCM sends the panel the command to switch the warning light off. During this check stage the behaviour of the gauge should be as defined in the previous paragraph ("gauge behaviour at key-on"). Through the effect of the warning light coming on, the pointer is not in the end of scale position during the check stage.

If the warning light on conditions were present at the key-on (engine coolant temperature overheating and warning light already on at the previous key-off), the c.c.m. keeps the command to switch the warning light on activated and the instrument panel continues to keep the warning light in an ON state and places the pointer in the end of scale position.

Indicator recovery logic (step motor)

If the indicator stepping motors are losing steps, due, for example, to: transportation/movement, installation of the panel on the vehicle or as a result of serious mechanical and electro-magnetic stresses that have occurred whilst the vehicle was being driven on the road or whilst it was stationary.

There is a "return to zero" logic for all the gauges (partial or complete recovery) at each key-on and key-off operation

This logic also provides for the "return to zero" of all the gauges (complete recovery) each time the battery is connected (+BATT.)

When the gauges are in the "normal operating" positions, this logic guarantees that any movements/fluctuations of the gauges are not visible to the user.

ENGINE OIL LEVEL gauge (only for JTD engine)

The engine oil level gauge function indicates engine oil level at start-up on the instrument display.

The gauge is equipped with a special circuit that controls a hot wire oil level sensor.

The information is displayed: on the display (odometer) on the LOW version, on the reconfigurable matrix display on the HIGH version.

Display of the signal

LOW VERSION

At key on, the message OIL is displayed on the lower part of the odometer for 10 seconds. Six digital squares on the upper part of the display gradually light up to show the amount of oil present in the engine. With al the squares lit, the oil level is at maximum.

As the oil level drops, the squares in the upper part gradually go out.

When the oil level is at minimum, the squares in the upper part are all out and the underlying dashes flash at a rate of 0.5 Hz.

If the oil level is higher than a critical value, above the maximum level, the message “HIGH OIL” is displayed for 10 seconds.

If a break or short-circuit is present in the indicator circuit at key-on, the word OIL flashes for 10 second at a rate of 0.5 Hz and the dashes disappear.

HIGH VERSION

At key on, the message engine oil level is displayed for 10 seconds. The amount of oil present in the engine is displayed by turning six bars on/off. The maximum oil level is represented by all the bars lit.

If the oil level is lower than the minimum specified level, the bars are all off and the message "minimum oil level" is displayed for 10 seconds. The bars are also all empty and the low oil level symbol appears in the warning light area.

If the oil level is above the maximum specified level, the bars will all be lit up and the "maximum oil level" message will be displayed for 10 secs.

If a fault is detected in the oil level sensor, the "oil level sensor fault" message will be displayed for 10 seconds.

Signal acquisition

The vehicle must be level for accurate signal acquisition. The barycentric position of the sensor nevertheless compensates for minor tilting of the vehicle.

The counter is zeroed the first time the battery is connected.

At the first key on, the oil level is ready (reading time equal to 1 second) and the result is shown on the display.

Afte reading, the counter is set to 20 minutes. During the key on period, the counter decreases by one unit per minute to a minimum value of 2 minutes.

At the next key off, the counter decreases from two down to zero.

At the next key on, and only if the counter is equal to zero, the system reads and stores the new value.

If the counter is still >0 at key on, it is compared with the previous reading and if:

  • the current reading is greater than or equal to the previous reading by 3 segments, measurement display notches, the reading is downloaded, stored and the counter is reset to 20 and the countdown starts again as before;
  • the current reading is less than 3 segments, measurement display notches, the reading is not stored and the level status corresponding to the last effective reading is displayed. The counter resets itself to 20 and begins the countdown again.

The EOBD (European On Board Diagnosis) system continuously diagnoses emission-related components on the vehicle and turns on a warning light on the control panel to indicate any deterioration in the components.

The aim of the system is to:

  • monitor system efficiency;
  • indicate an increase in emissions due to vehicle malfunction;
  • indicate the need to replace damaged components.

Timely intervention to repair the fault that caused the warning light to come on is an obligation that depends on the laws and Highway Code in the country where the car is driven.

The instrument calculates the trip data as follows:

Distance travelled

The distance travelled by the vehicle from the beginning of the mission is indicated, i.e. since the user reset the counter by pressing the dedicated key. The reading is consistent with the display on the mileometer.

When the maximum possible mileage value is reached, the mileage display resets to zero automatically. A total TRIP computer reset is then performed.

The mileage reading is displayed with the following characteristics:

  • range between 0-4999.9 km
  • resolution equal to 0.1 km
  • update of display: every 0.1 km - The function is active from key on.

Trip time

The trip time shows the time elapsed from the start of the mission, i.e. since the user reset the counter by pressing the TRIP key or an automatic reset occurred

Each time the battery is reconnected and at the beginning of each mission, the display shows "00:00", after which the calculated value is displayed.

At each key-on, the value stored at the previous key-off is displayed, except for the TRIP counter that automatically resets after the vehicle is parked for 2 h

If the vehicle is parked with the engine off (key off), the accumulated trip counter stops but does not reset to zero. The count resumes as soon as the vehicle sets off again (next key on - engine running).

The function is active from key on, with the engine running.

The mission time is displayed in hh mm with the following characteristics:

  • range between 00:00 and 99:59
  • resoluition equal to 1 min.
  • display updated every minute
  • data update every second

When the maximum possible value is reached (99.59) the mileage display resets to zero automatically. A total TRIP computer reset is then performed

Average speed

The average speed is calculated from the beginning of the mission, as a ratio between distance travelled and trip time.

Vm = distance travelled/trip time

The calculation is performed only with the engine running.

Each time the battery is reconnected and at the beginning of each mission, the display shows "----" for the first 10 seconds (10s), after which the calculated value is displayed.

At each key-on, the value stored at the previous key-off is stored, except for the TRIP B counter that automatically resets after the vehicle is parked for 2 h.

The displayed average speed must be equal to"----", whenever:

  • the user resets the counter by pressing the dedicated button.
  • the distance travelled and/or trip time parameters are reset.

The average speed value is displayed with the following specifications:

  • range between 0 - 250 km/h *- resolution equal to 0.1 km/h
  • calculation precision: = 0.1 km/h
  • display updated every 10 s ± 0.1s (10s)

Average fuel consumption

Average fuel consumption measn the ratio between distance travelled since the start of the mission and number of litres consumed since the start of the mission.

Cm = distance travelled/litres of fuel consumed

The control panel downloads the fuel consumption signal via the B-CAN network and processes it to divide it by the distance travelled since the start of the mission.

At the start of a new mission, due to battery disconnection or TRIP computer reset, the average fuel consumption value is reset to the individual predefined average standard fuel consumption value for the vehicle/engine version.

A weighting to be attributed to the above initial value to avoid excessive changes in the reading shown during the first few minutes of the mission.

After this, the reading tends to represent the true mission fuel consumption.

The value displayed is equal to "----" for the first 10 seconds, after which the figure calculated is displayed.

At each key-on, the value stored at the previous key-off is displayed, except for the TRIP counter that automatically resets after the vehicle is parked for 2 h

Per consumo istantaneo s'intende il valore di litri di carburante consumati dal veicolo nella missione il dato viene calcolato sulla base del segnale di consumo trasmesso dalla centralina controllo motore,. The instrument panel acquires the consumption signal via the B-CAN

When the battery is connected, the value displayed should be equal to "----" for the first 10 seconds, after which the figure calculated is displayed.

For the calculation of the instant consumption, in order to avoid the value displayed varying too much, a "predefined average standard consumption" figure is used (personalized for the vehicle/engine type); afterwards the weight of the initial reading gradually becomes less important and the consumption figures are used.

Range

The range indicates the estimated distance (in km or miles) that the car could travel with the fuel currently in the tank, assuming the mission is continued applying the same driving style (same fuel consumption conditions). This value is calculated using information received from:

Body Computer:

  • fuel level (as a percentage of a full tank);

Engine management control unit:

  • reference fuel consumption calculated by the control unit

Value storedi in the instrument panel:

  • fuel tank capacity (litres)

Range in km is calculated by multiplying the reference fuel consumption by the number of litres of fuel in the tank or by dividing the litres of fuel present in the tank by average mission fuel consumption.

When the battery is connected, the value displayed should be equal to "----" for the first 30 seconds, after which the figure calculated is displayed.

At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is stored.

During the mission, the displayed range is updated by amounts proportional to the difference between the displayed value and the calculated value to avoid excessive fluctuations.

More specifically:

  • if the difference between the calculated value and the displayed value exceeds 40 km, the change in displayed range is equal to one sixth of the difference.
  • if the difference between the calculated value and the displayed value is between 6 km and 39 km, the change in displayed range is equal to 3 km
  • if the difference between the calculated value and the displayed value is less than 6 km, the change in displayed range is equal to 1 km

When the fuel level is on the reserve, i.e. reserve warning light on, and range is lower than 50 km, no more data is transmitted to the user (but the range count continues). In other words, the display shows the message "attention - refuelling necessary" + symbol for 20 s followed by "----" .

Even if the trip screen is not active, when the above limit is reached (range lower than 50 km), the message is displayed as described above and then the display returns to the screen active at the time the anomaly event occurred.

If the vehicle is refueled, the new range value is immediately displayed.

When fuel has been added, if the range is still lower than the required limit (50 km), no reading is displayed and the indication "----" remains.

The refuelling information is downloaded as described in the chapter on the fuel level gauge.

If the vehicle is at a standstill ( < 3 km/h) with the engine running (e.g. traffic lights - traffic jam), the last value before the vehicle was parked is shown for 3 minutes after which the indication "----" appears.

The display is returned to normal operating mode with vehicle speed > 3 km/h. The range value is updated taking into account the fuel consumed while the vehicle is parked, considering driving style prior to the halt (last 5 minutes).

The range calculation is always active

The range value is displayed with the following specifications:

  • calculation precision: = 1 km)
  • resolution: 1 km
  • display updated every 30 s ± 0.1s
  • max reading equal to 1999 km
  • min indicate value equal to 50 km, after which the following indication is shown "----"

Recovery

If the computer is not connected to the B-CAN network, all the TRIP counters show the message "not available" instead of a reading together with a description of the data characteristics.

If the speed sensors are faulty, all the TRIP counters display dashes "----" together with the data characteristics of each item (km for range , km/h for average speed etc.).

If the fuel sensor is faulty, dashes "----" are shown only for Range and Average fuel consumption together with descriptions of each data characteristic.

If the fault disappears, the count of the various items continues in their different ways and the values downloaded prior to the mission are not reset and the mission is not restarted.

Fault display logic

If a message and associated symbol are displayed:

  • the written message remains for 20 seconds and then disappears. It then reappears with the symbol at the next key on for the above time (until the underlying fault is removed). If the fault disappears during the display cycle, the message + symbol are displayed for a minimum time of 2 seconds.
  • The symbol is maintained in the dedicated area (bottom right) of the display and must stay there until the underlying fault cause is resolved.
  • then, when the display cycle is complete, the screen prior to the fault event reappears unless it was displayed in the dedicated area of the display occupied by the fault symbol.

  • Normal operating condition: the instrument panel is only enabled to signal the fault message if the engine rpm remains above 200 rpm (lower threshold)

DISPLAY LOGIC IF MORE THAN ONE FAULT IS PRESENT SIMULTANEOUSLY

If more than one fault is present simultaneously, they are displayed for 5 seconds each in rolling mode. The overall display time is related to the underlying logic and thus they must remain for 20 seconds (per fault) until the message + symbol display cycle has concluded. After this only the symbols will be displayed.

If another fault arises during the display of a fault message (message + symbol cycle), the most recent fault supersedes the previous fault only after the latter has been displayed for 2 seconds. The subsequent display mode is still the rolling type described previously (overall time 20 s). If several display cycles are in progress, only screens consisting of message + symbol are displayed in rolling mode. When one of the cycles concludes (after 20 s), the other cycles must also conclude before display of the warning lights alone reappears in rolling mode.

If the events do not occur simultaneously, the most recent fault is displayed in the same way as described for display of the first fault, i.e. the message + symbol persist for 20 seconds. After this, the message disappears and the symbol alone remains and the display alternates with the symbols already present in rolling mode (5 seconds each).
